utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Marcus, are you ready to proceed? And may I remind you that the -- what we did in the last five minutes yesterday, that is, to try to find out what the expert witness really wants to say in terms of facts or an assessment of how it should be under the rules should -- if we keep that in mind, that might save a lot of time, because we don't have to explore a lot of factual issues which, in fact, are not there. Would you therefore always pay attention to that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, I would like to remind you again that you are not bound -- that you are bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus will now continue her cross-examination, but only after she has given us an indication as to how much time she would still need.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, my original estimate, as you know, was five hours. I believe I used an hour and 48 minutes on Thursday. Now, the Stanisic team's cross did not extend that time, so I would say that I would use about three hours today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I do, I would just like to put one -- mention one thing on the record, which can easily be done in the presence of the witness, with your leave, Your Honours. It pertains to a list of bar table documents that we received yesterday from the Simatovic Defence. The only thing I would like to mention about that is that the chart, the table of 160 documents, did not contain any information about origin or about the relevance of those documents. I wanted to make mention of this. I don't know what the time-frame is for that. But we cannot, of course, begin -- we appreciate being notified of which documents, but we cannot begin the process of preparing our responses until we have that information from the Simatovic Defence. I just wanted to inquire as to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the list which starts with the footnote number and then the 65 ter number? Or are you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The footnote number, I think that pertains to the MUP expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What I'm talking about now is something quite apart from the instant witness. This was an e-mail that we received about the bar table documents which come, I believe, from the Borojevic report. So it's a separate issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the first working day after the break you remember that we said, we promised, that we would inform you of which documents from the Borojevic report would be part of our bar table motion. We sent that list so that our colleagues could prepare themselves with greater ease. Our list hasn't yet been completed. It will soon be completed. And naturally it will then contain all the information that my colleague has requested. This is something that we did in advance in order to facilitate the work of the Prosecution in accordance with the instructions that we received from you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we said come as quickly as possible with at least what the documents are when you're still further preparing. So I take it that you'll receive that as soon as possible. And where you have already relevant information, that you could start perhaps working already.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was the specific task that the Simatovic Defence gave you with respect to the Franko Simatovic section of your report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of his professional file, it was necessary for me to reconstruct his career in the service, and that is, in fact, what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So they specifically asked you to reconstruct his career in the service, based on his personnel file; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the report, all the issues I explained in detail. And I will read this out for the sake of precision. In paragraph 7, on page 5, it says that on the basis of the personnel file I analysed the professional biography of Simatovic, his career path in the service, the positions he was appointed to, the rank he was conferred, his annual assessments. I do apologise to the interpreters. I'll repeat this. On the basis of his personnel file, I analysed Franko Simatovic's CV, including his admission to the career in the service; the workplace to which he was assigned; the titles, or rather, the ranks that he held; his annual evaluations; and the positions he had relative to the internal SDB or RDB and/or MUP of Serbia hierarchy. So that would be my precise answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So if you had not had Mr. Simatovic's personnel file, would you have been able to prepare, based on your own expertise - your own research, your own access to documentation - would you have been able to prepare a section on Franko Simatovic's duties and responsibilities, as part of an expert report?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly wouldn't have been able to do that in this detail and this precisely. No one's career path can be reconstituted without having access to that person's personnel file, and that is valid for Franko Simatovic and for anyone else, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, before I move on from the section -- from the Simatovic section on to the JATD section, I have a few questions I'd like to ask you about the documents which we provided to you, which were listed in a chart, and which are documents which contain the signature or initials of Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 6488. I also have the hard copies, if, with the Chamber's leave, perhaps the Court Officer to give the hard copy of the charts back to the witness, in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I know a week has passed since you reviewed these materials, but do you recall reviewing the documents in the binder, documents which contain the signature or initials of Mr. Simatovic? I believe it's the third chart in that package of charts that I'm speaking about. It has a yellow tab. The third tab. Do you recall looking at these documents?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When? Which period do you have in mind? When did I have a look at them?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm talking about last week when we provided you with these materials.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely. I'd have to have a look at the documents in order to answer that question. No one could remember this. You didn't give me much time to have a look at the documents. I don't know these documents by heart. If you let me have a look at the documents, I'll answer your question. I assume that I did have a look at them, but I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I certainly will not put you on the spot with any particular document in that way. You have them in front of you. If there's anything that you feel you need to consult in order to answer the questions I'll ask, then, of course, you will have the time to do that. I just wanted to confirm for the record that these are the materials that I provided to you. This is one part of the materials that we provided to you, which you reviewed last week. That was my first question: Just to confirm that these are the materials that you reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that I looked at these documents. There were three --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, did you look -- did you look at binders which look very similar to what you have in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Three binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Ms. Marcus will go in more specific questions. And then if you then come across any document which you say, I don't remember that I've seen it, please tell us and have a closer look at it. Wait for the questions that Ms. Marcus will put to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, based upon your knowledge of and familiarity with DB documentation, and as an experienced researcher, if you had had the documents in the binder containing Mr. Simatovic's signature to consult in preparing your report, your professionalism would have obliged you to compare the roles and tasks and responsibilities of Mr. Simatovic, that he was carrying out according to those DB documents, with the DB documents contained in Mr. Simatovic's personnel file, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. I would have compared all the documents available, including those ones, the ... there's no question about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And so it flows from that, then, that you would have drawn inferences and conclusions about Mr. Simatovic's roles and responsibilities based on all the documents you had at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we discussed this issue on Thursday. On Thursday there was a discussion about the issue. The Prosecution has asked whether the expert's conclusions would have been different if he had had documents initialed by Franko Simatovic that seem to relate to the JATD. But for the expert witness to change his opinion, he would have to examine the entire field. In addition to the documents that have Franko Simatovic's initials, he would have to examine hundreds of other documents initialed by others or signed by others. He would have to examine orders from others that concern the same subject matter in order to reach a different conclusion about the position and role that Franko Simatovic may have had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there's some confusion at this moment. Let me try to explain to you what, in my view, the confusion is. The witness has explained to us that he was given -- he was tasked to analyse the documents, he said, personnel file and set out clearly this was the position at that time, that's the rules that regulate this, et cetera, et cetera, which, as far as I understand the witness, does not include any research on whether or not Mr. Simatovic acted in accordance with what he was tasked with, on paper. That is, position, ranks, are you stationed here; then, okay, then you're supposed to work there, and not perhaps somewhere else. But I did not understand from the answer of the witness that he was also tasked with checking whether the activities, as they appear in other documentation, not in the personnel file, whether that fits into his formal position and into the rules and regulation which govern that formal position. So, Ms. Marcus, I think when you asked the question to the witness, If you would have looked at all this, would you have analysed that and that and that, that it's not only different material, but it would also have been another task. The task being: Would you please analyse and research whether what we can see from the documentary evidence as apparently the activities Mr. Simatovic, whether that fits in what you have analysed. So not only different documents, but also a different task. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, and I do apologise for this request, I would like to respond, but outside of the hearing of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We could -- and you'd like to do that now, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Milosevic, I have to ask you to briefly leave the courtroom, then, but remain stand by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution's position with respect to this expert report is essential as follows, especially with respect to the portions on Mr. Simatovic and on the JATD: The Simatovic Defence provided to the witness a very carefully selected, limited selection of DB documentation. The witness took that on its face. That's what he looked at. I don't know whether he asked for anything else. I was going to ask him if he asked for any other materials. Our position is that his professionalism should have led him to ask for other materials, especially where he was given excerpts of personnel files. And he may not - I don't know yet until I ask - whether he asked to review the remainder of those personnel files. So in our view what the Simatovic Defence did was they gave him a selection, and directly based on that selection he produced an expert report that is focussed because of the selection provided to him by the Simatovic Defence. Now, if -- and that is our position especially, Your Honours, with respect to the JATD section, but I submit that it applies also to the Franko Simatovic section. Now, I understand what Your Honours are saying. His task was to analyse the personnel file. But as we have here, if this expert report is going to come into evidence, the way it reads, it's not qualified in any way. It's not limited in conclusions that can be drawn from it. The only relevance the report can possibly have to their case is that the -- what ought to have happened was actually what happened. Otherwise it has simply no relevance. So what I'm --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What I was planning to do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There, I think, there's the big disagreement. The report says what it says, and that's not much. I would agree with you. But, apparently, the Prosecution - and, Mr. Petrovic, if you again draft, a chart, I would use the word "Prosecution" rather than "persecution," because that might be misunderstood, that's the chart you apparently sent yesterday - if you say it's of limited probative value, I would agree with you. Because -- and that's apparently -- apparently the Prosecution fears that the Chamber would understand this expert report as reflecting reality beyond the paper reality of the rules and the decisions to appoint. Apparently the Prosecution fears that the Chamber would understand that if someone is tasked with A, B, C, D, and E, that the person appointed to perform those tasks did so. If we look at the expert report, what you could conclude is that he was appointed in a position where A, B, C, and D were the task -- in a position where A, B, C, D, and E were what someone was supposed to do when performing his duties in that position. Nothing more; nothing less. So, therefore, whether he did that or not, whether he did X, Y or Z or whether he did X, Y, and Z next to A, B, C, D, and E or whether he did not do A, B, C, D, and E at all and whether he did M and O, that -- the report doesn't answer those questions. And what you said is that it's therefore -- it gives support to the extent that the Chamber is now able to verify what the tasks and duties were for someone appointed in such a position, but does not in any way - and I think the witness has repeated that five, ten, 15, 20 times by now - that he does not give any insight in what actually that person appointed in that position did or did not. And it seems that you want to explore: Would not -- would your position not have been different, Mr. Expert, if you would have known that and that and that? It's my expectation that the witness would say, No, still these are the rules which regulate what someone appointed in such a position was supposed to do. Whether he did it or not, the witness has no idea, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On this point, Your Honour, if I might just respond. What I'm actually seeking to do on the matter of Mr. Simatovic is not show him what actually -- is not to ask him about evidence of what actually took place, but, rather, to present to him the same kind of documents that he reviewed in drawing his conclusions as to the -- what ought to have been done. So in other words, if he had these documents with the same task he was given, Your Honour - just bear with me for a second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If -- with the same task that the witness was given, not to -- not to analyse what actually happened, but to analyse what it appears Mr. Simatovic's roles and tasks and responsibilities were, if he had had these documents, his analysis of the roles and tasks and responsibilities would also have been different, regardless of any knowledge of it actually being carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So -- so what we would then expect, and it has got nothing to do with whether he should have reviewed other material, whether it would have affected his conclusions, what you'd like to say is, If your task is to take care of the weekly payment of subordinates, if that's your task - and then you show him a document where he ordered hamburgers for his neighbourhood - and say does this fit into that task? That's apparently the kind of questions you -- what we see him do here, ordering hamburgers, is that -- how does that fit in your task to take care of the daily -- of the weekly payments for your subordinates? That's the kind of -- of course, this is not --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- an example from reality. But I'm trying to understand that we do not dwell into any area which the witness just doesn't have -- looked at. And apart from that, sometimes there may be some -- some areas where could you have some doubt. But if he buys a tank or an airplane, I don't need a witness to explain to me that buying an airplane is not the same as taking care of the weekly payments of your subordinates. Sometimes it's obvious. There may be matters where you say, Well, is there any way that you could explain it in such a way that it would fit into the tasks; if not, then it apparently falls outside the scope of that task. But sometimes there may be an explanation, so as to -- to better understand why this was not, not outside the scope of his task. But I want to -- we have listened now for days and days extensively to all kind of questions that were put to the witness, where he finally says, I didn't look at it. And if you say, Well, then it may be of limited support for the Simatovic Defence, that may be true or not true, but that's the choice the Simatovic Defence makes. If they think that it greatly assists the Chamber to know all the regulations and to look at this kind of paperwork only, then we'll see what we'll do with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I'm simple seeking to do is to challenge and contextualise the witness's evidence, which is, in fact, my job to do that. So the witness has presented certain evidence. I -- I hear what the Chamber is saying about what his task was. I hear from him what he was saying. In my first few questions he agreed that had he had these materials he would have had to consider them and compare and come to different conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not -- I -- I would like to put further questions to the witness that would -- within what he was tasked with, it would not have led him to any conclusion, because he was not tasked to find out whether documentation on what Mr. Simatovic did fit into what he was supposed to do. The task was limited to describe to us what a person appointed in position A is supposed to do as his task. And whether what he actually did fits into the picture was not his task, as I understand it. I can tell you that I would have further asked further questions about when he said, Yes, of course, I would have looked at those documents because they are irrelevant for his task. And we are giving him more documents and implicitly we're expanding his task by the way you proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will take the Chamber's instructions. I must respectively disagree that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first check it all that I ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: -- but I will do as Your Honours instruct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Overlapping speakers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My colleagues, although there's no fundamental disagreement with my -- with my analysis, by majority would give you a bit more room. So, therefore, I would join in that. And, Ms. Marcus, if you say that you respectively disagree, then I always have to check whether I'm performing my role as a Presiding Judge appropriately, and you have a -- again, on the theoretical level -- and, of course, the whole issue is caused by the witness using often language which doesn't reflect what he really wants to present. His assessment of the reality, as you read it now and then, asked about it, seems not -- has not to do anything with reality, but, rather, about rules and appointments and -- But, therefore, I'll be cautious in further intervening. Could the witness be brought into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I just want to -- your answer to my last question wasn't recorded because we began our discussion, so I just want to ask you that question before I proceed. I had asked you if you had had, for example, these documents in analysing the role and responsibilities and tasks of Mr. Simatovic, if you had had these as well, you would have compared them with the official tasks he was assigned as per his personnel file. You said, in principle, Yes, I would have compared all the documents available including those ones. There's no question about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are talking about a collection of 45 different documents which depict only Simatovic's initials. I would like to hear exactly what was it that Simatovic did and that was initialed instead of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, Mr. Petrovic, have you an opportunity to re-examine the witness at a later stage. We are -- you're now entering in a debate. You can oppose, you can object against the question. We are, at this moment, at a level where the witness is asked about what he think he would have done if he would have seen those documents and what he considers would have been his task when he would have been provided with those documents, and that's the question the witness should answer first. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One sentence, Mr. Petrovic. But ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking for a very precise qualifications of the documents that are being shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is about the documents given to him to look at. That's what we're talking about now. And if, when we are proceeding, specific documents will be discussed, we'll have them on our screen and we'll look at them very precisely. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus. Perhaps you better repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I will. I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, before I repeat the question, just for your information --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question. You don't have to repeat it. I can answer immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer? I would have certainly looked at all the documents; however, my report would be absolutely the same because for me only the documents within his personnel file would bear some weight. I would have looked at everything else out of curiosity or for some other reason. However, in keeping my task, I did what I was supposed to do. And I would have done the same again, irrespective of any other kind of documents that I might have seen. I would have always used the personnel file as the only relevant set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify that before I move on, just so we understand your answer: I do understand that the task you were given was to analyse Mr. Simatovic's roles and responsibilities as per his DB personnel file. I understand that. Now, if you had been asked, without it being limited to that as your source, to analyse Mr. Simatovic's roles and responsibilities, as an expert, then you would agree with me that these other documents which also come from DB personnel files - every one of them is an official document from a personnel file from a DB official personnel file, so they are the same kinds of documents - that these would have been relevant to a proper expert analysis of Mr. Simatovic's roles and responsibilities. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have a wrong qualifications of the documents. It says from the official personnel documents of the DB. I will not go into the documents. I just want to say that the qualification, as given, does not really correspond to the nature of those documents. I just want this to be clear and on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you explain your answer, why you wouldn't agree with what I suggested?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I reconstruct a career path of a person in service, you use personnel documents, not operative or any other documents. The only relevant documents are those that can be found in somebody's personnel file. It is impossible to reconstruct anything based on hundreds of thousands of documents. I don't know what you mean. And I repeat, although I believe that everybody in this room understands that, only the personnel file of the accused in this case were relevant for reconstructing his career path. This is my professional opinion, and I'm sure that you don't have to agree with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you say the report would have been the same. Nevertheless, Ms. Marcus wants to explore certain matters with you which are closely related to the career path, as you researched it, on the basis of the files that were given to you. Ms. Marcus, if you would start with that, then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I -- I don't want to debate this. I just want to make sure that we completely understand. The report, the way it's written, doesn't qualify it and say it's only about his career path. It talks -- it -- it does say that you were -- that you had a methodology which permitted you to conclude what Mr. Simatovic's de jure and de facto responsibilities were. Now, I know that you have said that you don't have information about facts. I accept that completely. But these documents demonstrate Mr. Simatovic carrying out duties that go beyond what you set out in the report. Whether he did it or not, again, is another question that you may or may not know. But if the documents are taken on their face, as you took the other DB documents on their face, they suggest duties and responsibilities which are outside the duties and responsibilities you set out. That's the basis for my putting these questions to you. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really apologise. We're talking about duties and tasks. Could my learned friend please specify which documents and which tasks arise from these specific documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we are not yet at that point. That is to further develop by Ms. Marcus. At this moment we're only on the rather theoretical level, what Ms. Marcus intends to do and what she would have expected, rightly or wrongly, that the witness would have done. So, therefore, let's wait and see when we come to specific documents, where, as I understand it, Ms. Marcus would like to explore, which she expected the expert would have done even of his own initiative, to explore to what extent what we see in another document fits into the picture which we find in the report. And one of the reasons being for making this exercise, that the report, although very much focussing on appointments, rules, regulations, et cetera, here and there, goes already beyond that. Ms. Marcus, is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. Mr. Petrovic, I would like you to be -- to limit your objections to the bare minimum. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what I'm going to do --

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I believe that you put a question to me and I didn't answer because there was an objection. You asked me something about whether I agreed with you or not. I said I didn't. I don't know whether I have to repeat the answer that I provided or whether I actually answered your question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you were then asked to explain why you disagreed. But, Ms. Marcus, perhaps you phrase a question. Whether you rephrase it or whether it's a new question, I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I had actually, just before we stopped, I had just explained, in fact, to you what led me to asking that question. I had explained that this documentation taken on its face presents different duties and responsibilities. Not asking you about the facts. But taking the documents on their face, as you do throughout your report, you take the DB documents on their face, and you analyse them and draw conclusions. I'm suggesting that these documents, taken on their face, demonstrate duties and responsibilities of Mr. Simatovic which were outside those that you presented. That was the basis for my putting the questions to you. And then I asked you whether you understood that. If you'd like to respond, please do, and then I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question. If the Chamber agrees with this method of questioning, I will repeat -- I will answer. I repeat: If I were asked to do this report again, my analyse would have been the same because I used documents from the accused's personnel file. Again, I repeat, if you want me to, I can answer all your questions along this line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are supposed to listen carefully to what Ms. Marcus asks and then answer that question to the best of your abilities. Ms. Marcus, I think the sooner we get to the concrete level, the sooner we can leave behind us this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm doing that now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic, I'm going to show you certain of these documents and ask you specific questions. I'm going to fold that into the next part of my -- of my questioning. So let me ask you: What -- with respect to the JATD section, what were the instructions given to you by the Simatovic Defence in preparing your report with respect to the JATD section?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to be precise, let me quote from my own report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. If you're just going to quote back to us paragraph 8, then we all have that. If that would be your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now my next question. Did the Simatovic Defence ask you to include a section in your report on the JATD, or did you determine that to be an important chapter for your report on your own?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly an important chapter, and the -- the report would not have been complete without that -- that chapter. I believe that this is self-evident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question. The question was whether you were specifically asked to include a JATD paragraph, or that you included it because you considered it important. Now, you've explained to us that you consider it important. You have not answered the question whether you were specifically asked to do that or whether it was just on the basis of your own assessment of the importance that you included it. Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence asked for that, inter alia. And even if they hadn't, I would still believe that this chapter is very important.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On the 2nd of May, at page 18948, Mr. Petrovic asked you: "When drawing up your report, did you have at your disposal any documents relating to the establishment of the unit for anti-terrorist action JATD, or did you make your conclusions about the establishment of this unit in some other ways?" You answered: "I had to draw my conclusions in a round-about way, because I did not see the decision to establish the JATD specifically. Rather, based on personnel files and other decisions, including letters of appointments and assignment and the payrolls, I reconstructed the moment when they were established." On the 7th of May you sent to us, through the Victim/Witness Unit the information that to the best of your recollection the Simatovic Defence had provided you with four JATD decisions on employment and salary, all dated 1994 and all coming from separate DB personnel files, and that they had provided you with JATD payment lists from 1993 to 1995. You also informed us that you have seen many other rules and documents - you estimated at least 100 - provided to you by the Defence but that you did not use them, as they were irrelevant. On the 7th of May, the Simatovic Defence informed the Prosecution and the Chamber that: "Milosevic was provided with per diem lists for JATD and various decisions of employment status in JATD." Now, here are my questions: Did the Simatovic Defence spontaneously provide you with documentation relating to the JATD from which you should draw your inferences, or did you ask them for documentation in order to write that chapter?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have a problem with my learned friend quoting from Mr. Milosevic's document. It says: "Documents that I was provided by the Defence." That's bullet point 3. "In drafting my analysis, I reviewed a lot of documents and letters, at least 100, as well as books, brochures, and articles, that were offered to me by the Defence or which I obtained through my individual research works in archives and libraries." The second part of the sentence, meaning, "which I obtained through my own individual research work," was not read out to the witness in -- as part of the question that my learned friend put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, that second part relates to other laws and rules and regulations. I'm talking about the DB documents. It's true that I quoted part of it. I was focussing on the DB documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Milosevic, my question: Did the Simatovic Defence provide you with the documents from which you should draw your conclusions on the JATD section, or did you ask for them, for that documentation, in order to draft that chapter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see in the report, some of the documents were provided to me by the Defence, and some were obtained through my own individual research. I'm not sure whether you quoted my words properly in your question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, could you just -- there's no need to add fuel to this little fire which started a minute ago. The question was -- you say documents were provided to me. I obtained some documents through my own individual research. Did you ask for any additional problems [sic] to the Simatovic Defence, where you said, I don't have documents in this area, you have not provided me with those documents, do you have them and could you provide them to me? Did you ask for any additional documents from the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't ask for anything else. I tried to find the rules on organisation of the JATD and the regulations on salaries; however, I was not able to find the two, nor was I provided the two. And then -- maybe I should explain, actually. I looked at a certain number of decisions on appointment in the JATD as well as decisions on determining the coefficient for salaries. Those were the documents that I looked, nothing else. And since they were all of the same format, they always involved the same rules. I can tell you exactly what they were. Based on that, I drew an inference that those documents existed but I did not see them personally. In order to be precise, I will read from my analysis. I could not personally inspect those documents, because I never saw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't think that was part of the question I did put to you. I would seek -- like to seek one clarification. You said: "I didn't ask for anything else. I tried to find the rules on the organisation of the JATD and the regulations on salaries; however, I was not able to find the two, nor was I provided ..." My question was: Did you ask for it? Did you ask the Simatovic Defence: These and these documents which I was trying to find, I did not manage to find; do you have them? Could you provide them to me? Did you ask that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if they had had those documents, they would have given them to me. It's clear, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Sometimes people make mistakes. Sometimes people are not aware of your position that it's relevant. So, therefore, I would invite you -- if I ask you: Did you ask for it? The first I expect you to do is to say "yes" or "no," whether you asked or not. And then if you want to explain why you didn't ask for it, that's the second step. But let's focus, first of all, on answers on the question. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm going to ask you very specific questions about this very issue, so please bear with me. If we need further clarification, we will ask. Now, had -- if the Simatovic Defence had not given you those decisions, those few decisions on appointment and the decisions determining the coefficient for salaries, if they had not provided you with that, and in the absence of the rules on the organisation or formation of the JATD, would you have been able to put together a chapter of your expert report on the JATD?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have been able to do that with such precision. I wouldn't have been able to refer to certain fundamental documents relating to its establishment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And the documentation that you were provided with by the Simatovic Defence you deemed sufficient in order to write your analysis, as an expert, on the rules governing the JATD; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given what I had available to me from earlier on, I thought that the documentation I had was quite sufficient and relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What do you mean what was available to you from earlier on? Are we talking still about the materials provided to you by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've been involved in research for several decades -- well, I don't want to exaggerate. So I already had information on the existence of the JATD. I didn't hear about the existence of the JATD from the Defence. When I was involved in research, I had certain information. I carried out research by consulting archives of various kinds, and so on and so forth. I can't say that everything I learned about the JATD was something that I learned because the Defence provided me with certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 371 of your report, you quote the 1977 Law on Internal Affairs of Serbia. Specifically, you reference the provisions of the 1977 law which state that the republican secretary of the interior may form special police units. This 1977 law was replaced by the 1991 law that you cite in the next paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So, actually, the provisions regarding the formation of special police units in the 1977 law are not applicable in the post-1991 period; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, I said that you could see that the special police units weren't created in 1991. They also existed in a previous period on the basis of a former law, an earlier law, but after the decision on creating special police units was adopted in 1993, those units were established. There was a legal basis that existed earlier on as well. That's what's important. It says which units were created in 1993 and where. But I don't think it's necessary for me to repeat what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to go through it to make sure we understand. When you -- in the next paragraph, that's paragraph 372, when you cite to the 1991 Law on Internal Affairs - for our purposes that's P1044 - you refer to the minister of the interior's role in specifying the purview of organisational units, their organisation, seats, and areas for which they are set up. You do not cite to where that law, the 1991 law, gives the minister of the interior the power to actually establish or form these special units. Under the 1991 law, who had the authority to establish special police units, as the 1977 law called them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister of internal affairs. And that is quite explicitly stated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What's explicitly stated is the role of the minister of internal affairs in establishing organisational units. Are you saying that organisational units and special police units are the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in the second sentence of paragraph 372, you describe the decision on the setting up of the special police units PJM. For our reference, that is Exhibit D87 in our case. You say that this decision was taken "In accordance with the above legal powers." Which presumably refers back to the 1991 law or the 1977 law. But upon looking at D87, it states that the decision is in accordance with the February 1992 rules of internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior. So from where did you derive that the decision was based on the 1991 law or the 1977 law?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Law on Internal Affairs, Article 6, item 2, from 1977. All sub-laws, as you are well aware, have to be in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, with respect to D87, that is, again, the decision on the formation of the PJM, which you discuss in these two paragraphs, the PJM was a unit of the public security; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all I would like to ask is for the witness to be shown D87 so that we are quite clear with regard to what is being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, would it help you to look at the document that we're talking about? That's the document, the decision, you quote in paragraph 372 of your report. Decision setting up the special police units. Would you like to see the document to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be good.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up D87.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall my question? My question was: The PJM was a unit of the public security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were units that came under the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I just have one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll return to that in one moment. Let me ask you my next question. You move from the discussion of the PJM, in your report, straight into the discussion of the JATD. You do not link in the text the discussion of the PJM with the JATD, so you leave us to interpret what you're trying to say. Now, presumably, you did that because you do see the formation of the PJM and the JATD to be somehow linked or comparable. Are you saying that the same rules apply to the formation of the PJM as to the JATD? Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a special chapter about the JATD. I'm not sure what I should say in relation to your interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, this is the -- these are the introductory paragraphs in the JATD section, so they must be in the JATD section for a reason. I'm trying to understand what you view as the connection between the PJM and the JATD, because you don't explain that. Are you saying that the same rules applied to the formation of the PJM as to the formation of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerns members of the reserve forces above all, and you could see that in the text and reach that conclusion. It's in the last sentence. But as a rule, well, I don't know how this should be interpreted in your opinion. I don't know how to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked to assist Ms. Marcus. You introduce, in a chapter which is under the title, "anti-terrorist operations unit, JATD," you have a kind of an introductory paragraph where you speak about the competences and powers of the minister of the interior to bring a decision establishing anti-terrorist units and special purpose police units. So you bring the two together in this paragraph, in these two paragraphs. And Ms. Marcus asks you whether it's the same or under the same rules and -- because there's not much of an explanation on why you introduce the special police units here. So please explain -- Ms. Marcus, that is what you're seeking, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's a clear question, Mr. ... Yes. Now, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason is that the special police units were formed by a decision on forming special police units that was signed by the minister of internal affairs. The JATD was also formed by the minister of internal affairs. The basis is the same. Article 6, paragraph 2. The Prosecution could have interpreted the language, but the basis here is legal, and I thought the legal issues were well known. So I was a bit confused by the question. So the basis for the formation of this -- these units is the same, and the way they are brought up to strength is the same. The legal basis is the same. It's Article 6, paragraph 2 on the Law on Internal Affairs. And it's the minister who takes that decision. I was a little confused, because what we are dealing with is the legal basis, and I wasn't quite sure what the purpose of your question was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That was exactly the purpose of my question. Thank you. So are you then saying that in your view the JATD was a formalisation of the PJM?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's a special unit formed by the minister of internal affairs on the basis of the same authority, and it had the same legal force as in the case of the other unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Your Honours would like to take a break, this might be an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if this is a good moment for you, then we would take a break and resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I'd like to instruct Madam Registrar to provisionally assign numbers to the list of source material to the Milosevic report that the Simatovic Defence intends to tender into evidence. I think I addressed already the matter that there's one document on your list, Mr. Petrovic, which is a marked, not admitted, document, which may need specific attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We provided information on that document that we think could be useful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar has already assigned a range of numbers. Perhaps we could put them on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The list of exhibits will receive numbers from D797 up and including D853, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then let me just have a look. I think D228 was suggested to be vacated. But since it has been used as a source now, I think it could be re-tendered if -- unless there's any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to have a look at that before expressing our position. But, of course, for an MFI at the moment, there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's not -- yes, it could then be MFI'd again under the same number for the time being, the status now being changed again. And whether or not there's any objection to admission, we'll hear from you before tomorrow, close of business?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Milosevic, we'll continue. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in paragraph 373 of your report, you describe the decision on the establishment of the JATD. Now, you do not footnote it, and now you've told us, both on the 2nd of May as well as earlier today, that you did not see that decision. You told us on the 2nd of May that you had to draw your conclusions in a round-about way. Would it not have been more accurate when making reference to a source that you have never seen to clearly set out that you have not actually seen it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that explicitly on a number of occasions here, and this is also that I put in the writing in the annex that you were provided with.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. But my point is, you provided the expert report and you didn't say that at all in the expert report. Have you been forthcoming when we asked you. But had we not asked, the way your expert stands you appear to have seen the decision. That's how it reads, any way. I'm just asking you from an academic professionalism point of view. Wouldn't it have been more accurate to say that you gleaned this in a round-about way rather than just stating the conclusion as if you had seen the decision?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't trying to reach such a conclusion. I didn't have any ill intentions. I wasn't attempting to plant anything on anyone. It's absolutely impossible to refer to this decision on -- on salaries if there is no such legal basis. This couldn't have been fabricated. Perhaps you don't like the style, but what I did is, in my opinion, in no way incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not have thought it more transparent if would you have written: The anti-terrorist -- it was, although I have not seep the decision itself, but on the basis of reconstruction, it must have been established by a decision, so and so, which I have not seen? Would that not be more transparent -- would that not have been more transparent than the way in which you present it in paragraph 373? I'm not talking about bad intentions. I'm not -- it's just transparency in a research report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's just a matter of style. I didn't have any ill intentions. I didn't want to plant anything. I quite simply didn't conceal anything. I wrote it down. It's quite clear. Well, perhaps the way it was put is something you don't like. That what you said is -- is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You've also not seen the job specification in the JATD which you also describe in that paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you have in mind exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You say that an integral part of the decision on the JATD was the job specification. Then you describe Article 37 of that document. I will ask you many detailed questions on that. But you didn't see the job specification itself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that document. Or, rather, I didn't see those rules, if that's what you're thinking of. Should I provide you with a more detailed explanation? I saw the job specifications, or, rather, schematic concerning the job specifications, and it had information on individuals who were appointed to certain positions. If that's what had you in mind, I saw that. But I didn't see the job specifications that form an integral part of what we are discussing. But if I haven't seen what I told you I saw, I wouldn't have known how many job specifications there were. Or, rather, how many workers there were. But this can change. However, the number of jobs remains the same. But there was this chart, this table.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to go into that and give you an opportunity in detail to speak about the chart you're referring to, which is P974, which I will call up in a few moments. Now, how did you know that the job specification was an integral part of the decision if you've never seen the decision and you've never seen the job specification?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's just the way things are. It has to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand what you base that assertion on. "... just the way things are."

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's that kind of a document. It contains that other document that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you presumed that, because you didn't see the documents, but you're presuming that. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a logical presumption that is based on analogy, and I derive my conclusions on what I did see.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 374 you describe incomplete records. You say: "Pursuant to incomplete records it may be concluded ..." et cetera. How can anything be concluded from incomplete records?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 374, it's a short paragraph, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It's in paragraph 373, not in 374. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I drew my conclusions based on what I did see. Therefore ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you mean when you said "incomplete records"? Which records are incomplete?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Records on the payment of per diems, for example.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was incomplete about them? I'm sorry, I'm just trying to understand. You used the term in your report "incomplete records." Which records were incomplete? I will go into which documents you consulted. I will go into that. But I just want to understand what you meant here when you said, "pursuant to incomplete records."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it is not for the first time. It is a frequent thing to happen that you seek eye contact with the Defence side before you answer a question. Would you please refrain from doing that. And would you please focus on the one who examines you, that is, Ms. Marcus. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this all right, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was the eye contact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It really wasn't my intention. It -- it is a misunderstanding for which I sincerely apologise. I will continue sitting like this. From the sources that I subsequently submitted, you can see exactly which months did those records cover. Per diems were paid out twice a month, and only the last month, the month of November, they were paid for the entire month. So I can't say that I had access to everything from beginning to end, and I drew my conclusions on -- on those things that I had available to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But you knew -- I'm not exactly sure why you're answering about the per diems. Is that -- that's what you meant to refer to when you said "pursuant to incomplete records," that refers only to the per diems?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you had per diems and you understood them to be incomplete. Is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had per diems but not for all of the months. I based my conclusions on those things I actually had.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you were told that they were incomplete, or you drew the conclusion that the records were incomplete?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had nothing after the month of November. Madam Prosecutor, it is all written down, and I really don't see anything ambiguous here. Some months, at the end of the period, were simply missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm not sure we understand each other. What you say here, and this is at the end of paragraph 337: "Pursuant to incomplete records, it may be concluded that the strength of this unit varied during the existence of the JATD, since workers on temporary contracts were admitted to it, but there is no data if all the work posts, according [sic] to the staffing specification, had ever been filled."

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not conclude whether all the posts were filled. The numbers varied. I really don't understand what is unclear in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What does that sentence have to do with the per diems?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the employees in that unit received per diems. And that is my indicator. That was at least the logic that I employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Among the documents upon which you apparently drew your conclusions in this paragraph, which we've learned in the course of your testimony and through, as you say, the annex of sources that you've sent to us on Monday, it appears you drew your conclusions from four individual documents that were provided to you by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: For the record, and I will use these individually, these are P2724, that is from the personnel file -- a document from the personnel file of Milan Radnic; P481, a document from the personnel file of Milenko Milovanovic; P475, a document from the personnel file of Janko Keres [phoen]; and P477, a document from the personnel file of Zoran Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you a few questions about these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have a copy of the first three in a hard copy in B/C/S, which can be handed to the witness. I've requested a copy of P477 as well, which will -- shall which will be provided hopefully soon. Can I ask the court usher to hand this out, please. For the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We're going to look at some of those documents a little bit later. For now I would just like to ask you to confirm that, in fact, those documents are the ones on which you relied in reaching your conclusions in paragraph 373.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a conclusion to the effect that a decision was passed by Zoran Sokolovic on the 4th of August, 1993, under number DT 012497. Based on those documents, I will explain in detail: I concluded that the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia established a unit for anti-terrorist activities and that the decision under which this was done bore number 012497; the decision was signed by the minister. And I also concluded that the minister of the interior on the 5th of January, 1994, also issued regulations on the payment of salaries of that unit. And that regulation was passed on the 5th of January. I also told you that there were a number of other similar decisions. I used the method of random sampling to see that all of those decisions referred to the same basic documents, the same decisions, and that's what I based my conclusions on. I don't know how else would I have made my inferences. I don't know what other method should I have employed. The method that I opted for was the method of random sampling. I don't know if there's any other method that could be considered more adequate than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm questioning the fact that you didn't explain the method in this section. So you didn't footnote to any of these documents. We found it out through informal communications and through asking you questions. But as your report stands, it's entirely not clear in here on what you drew these conclusions. Why did you not cite in your footnotes or your original bibliography these decisions that you consulted?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply did not consider this to be important. If this is my mistake, then it is my methodological mistake which was not based on any bad intention. But as far as I knew, oral testimony would be part of my overall evidence. I did not intend to hide anything. I didn't hide anything. I simply did not use the right method, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The whys are not -- the answers to the whys are not greatly assisting the Chamber. Let's just establish what was the case, that it was not sourced, and that -- you can think about that, whether that's good methodology, yes or no, but let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. And thank you to the Chamber for the permission to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to examine the entire DB personnel files for Milan Radonjic, Milenko Milovanovic, Janko Keres, and Zoran Rajic from which these documents were taken?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no need to do that. I never asked for those. I didn't see a purpose in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, of the four documents, the four decisions upon which you drew the inferences in paragraph 373, which of those four documents you referred to is the document from which you deduced that Article 37 contained the job specification for the JATD? Perhaps, until I have a hard copy of P477, we could call that up on the screen for the witness. Then he has the three hard copies in front of him and P477 on the screen. Then he'll have all four to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing on the screen. Were you referring some other screen? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, we had to wait a moment to call it up. So what you see in front of you is the fourth one that you mentioned to us. So you have three in hard copy and the fourth one is on your screen. Three of these documents all cite Article 5 of the decision on the formation of the JATD rather than Article 37. P475 is the only one which cites Article 37. What was Article 5 of the decision on the formation of the JATD; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't see why you are asking me this. What is the gist of all this? Why are you showing me this document? In my statement that I provided, I said that these are the three documents where this is explicitly spelled out, so -- and now you're showing me a fourth document. Why are you doing that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, please answer the questions. Do not comment on -- to -- to explore --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- explore the reasons why Ms. Marcus puts certain questions. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, these documents refer to bullet point or item 5, not Article 5. This makes a big difference and will probably change the question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the English translation on our screen, this -- it says item 37 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The B/C/S, I think, says "cilan [phoen]," which -- well, I'll leave it to the interpreters on that. I could change my question according to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Before I do that - and I will repeat my question - I would not want to confuse you Mr. Milosevic. The fourth document on the list that you provided to us on Monday is the one on the screen, so ... The Simatovic Defence had informed us of the first three that you in your hand. The fourth one, P477, is what you list as the fourth document from the personnel file of Zoran Rajic on your report that you provided to us. That's where I got it from. So this is the material that you informed us that you relied upon. That's why I'm asking you about it. Now, so, what I'm trying to do is to understand where you drew your conclusions from. You make assertions in the report; I'd like to know what the source for those assertions is. So you state -- you -- you state that Article 37 contained the job specification, but in three of the four documents, Article 5 - I should say, item 5 - is cited, not item 37. So I was asking you: Do you know what item 5 of the decision on the formation of the JATD was?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 5 refers to posts, or jobs. Item 5 lists all the posts and jobs, and each of those posts is then specified. For example, Milenko Milovanovic is assigned to 25/5. Janko Keres, item 5.6. This is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that is it not difficult to understand. I think what Ms. Marcus would like to know is where these documents refer to certain items. Whether you have ever seen the list containing those items, or whether you just said, Well, if it refers to item 5, it must be item 5. That goes without a lot of explanation. Have you ever seen the list of items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that I didn't. I drew my inferences in a round-about way. How many times do I need to repeat this? That's why I have shown you these decisions in order to demonstrate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, apparently what Ms. Marcus also would like to know is where you say that the job specification in the -- is found in -- found in Article 37. Have you ever seen Article 37? Or was it by mistake where you refer to Article 37 where you apparently want to refer to item 37, as we find it in the document on our screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This decision is somewhat different. This was issued to hire Zoran Rajic to work at the DB starting on the 1st of June, 1994, at job 1.7, according to the rule of job specifications. I saw this document, like we did all, because it was displayed here in the courtroom. I can't remember off the top of my head what this item was all about. But this document is not based on the decision on the establishment of the 8th JATD [as interpreted]. It is based on the regulation on the job specification of the State Security Department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's why I did not list that document as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So is the job specification under item 5 or item 37 of the decision on the formation of the JATD?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on item 5, the decision on the establishment of the JATD. That's my opinion. I concluded that on having perused other documents. And those are the documents --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't understand the last bit of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you repeat the last part of your answer because the interpreters were unable to hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in order to answer Ms. Marcus's question, I would have to say this. According to my opinion, item 5 is the decision on the establishment of the JATD, and based on that decision, the decision on the job specification of that unit was passed. And that's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, where you said Article 37 in -- in your -- in paragraph 373 in your report, you meant to say Article or item 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be precise, I'm going to read. The answer to your question is as follows: I believe that we're talking about item 5 on the decision of the establishment of the JATD, and in front of me, I have a document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is reading too fast. The interpreter cannot catch up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have to read more slowly because -- or to speak more slowly because interpreters cannot follow you. Could you please resume, well, let's say, a couple of lines ago. Perhaps where you said ... You said: "I believe that we are talking about item 5 of the decision on the establishment of the JATD ..." That's what you started. Could you then further complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right. That's the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In that same paragraph of your report, 373, you say: "Pursuant to Article 37" of the document that you have not seen, "there were 27 work posts in the JATD according to the staff specification with a total of 438 workers." How did you know that there were 27 work posts with a total of 438 workers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the attachments that I received from the Defence. Or, rather, I received from the Defence a representation of what things looked like.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up P974. It's probably also not to be broadcast to the public. And I have a hard copy for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this document is a tabular overview of posts in the JATD. We have been calling it the systematization document. That may not be the proper term for it, but that's how we've been calling it. Now, you did cite to this document in paragraph 376 of your report, so you did see this document. Is this the document that you're referring to on which you based the number 438 posts [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid further confusion: In 373, it's 27 work posts and 438 workers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And is this also the document from where you got Article, or item, 37?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I was looking at the document, and I failed to pay attention to your question. Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Absolutely. I just wanted to know if this was also the document where you got Article, or item, 37 from.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You talk about the job specification from item 37, and in this document the posts are listed under Article, or item, 37.

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, when I count the number of work posts, including those filled and unfilled, so regardless of whether there's a name appearing or not, I get approximately 207 posts. Now, I might have slightly miscounted, but there were certainly nowhere near 438 work posts -- workers' posts listed in here. So I'm a little bit confused both about the number 27 work posts and about the number 438 workers. Neither of those numbers appear to come from this document. Can you clarify for us where you got those numbers?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, under number 37 you can find that number, in fact, in column 2. As far as these numbers are concerned, though, I really cannot remember where they come from. I certainly did not invent them, but I can't remember where they come from now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you can't remember, then you can't remember. Now, in paragraph 374, you cite the rules on the salaries of workers in the JATD of the 5th of January, 1994. You also have not seen that document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
